label:
MFGM concentrate
(milk phospholipids)
note: The globule membrane is about the size of casein micelles, so casein has to be got out first; it can not just be filtered off.

about.text: The thin skin that wraps each fat globule in milk, rich in phospholipids and special proteins. Because churning breaks the globules, it ends up in the buttermilk, from which it is concentrated and dried for infant formula and supplements.

links.name: Frontiers in Nutrition 2021: Wang & Mu, Advancement on Milk Fat Globule Membrane

how.text: Washing the cream before churning lowers the dry matter of the buttermilk and so raises the phospholipid share.

links.name: Teagasc: characterisation and enrichment of buttermilk MFGM

steps.name: remove casein
steps.note: Casein is removed first, as MFGM fragments are about as big as casein micelles.

steps.name: polish
steps.note: Supercritical CO2 removes non-polar lipid and lifts the share of polar lipids.
Spray-drying cut phospholipid content by 38–41 % in one study.
